name: Fachtna

attributes.attribute: son of Nessa and heir of Ulster

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fachtna is an Irish hero name. Several heroes share it. Only one carries real weight in legend. That one is Fachtna the Great, the king of Ulster. He married the studious girl who was first called Assa, a word that meant gentle. The evil druid Cathbad killed her beloved tutors while trying to take her. Assa then became the warrior Nessa, a name that meant ungentle. Nessa bore a son who came forth with a worm in his hand. She said she had conceived while drinking from a glass that held two swimming worms, and so she was left with child by magic. Her son took her name and became Conchobar mac Nessa. Fachtna raised the boy. The son later took the throne of Ulster from that source.

okr.objective: Fachtna is an Irish hero king of Ulster tied to Nessa.
key_results: Fachtna Fáthach was king of Ulster.
He married Nessa, who was first named Assa.
The druid Cathbad killed her tutors.
Nessa's son Conchobar took the Ulster throne from Fachtna.
